title: Unified log enrichment orchestrator for service-boundary structured logs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a unified pre-ingest enrichment/orchestration layer for all Redwood service logs that standardizes structured fields, attaches distributed tracing identifiers, enforces tenant tagging, and routes to appropriate backends (Loki primary, ELK for compliance workspaces). Background: we currently have ad-hoc enrichers in several services and inconsistent field names (e.g., tenant_id vs org_id, request_id vs req_id). This causes mismatched dashboards and missing correlations between traces and logs. Scope: implement a lightweight enrichment orchestrator deployed as a cluster-level sidecar/daemonset and ingest pipeline stage (Vector/Fluent Bit) that performs: 1) normalization to the canonical structured schema, 2) enrichment from request headers (W3C traceparent, custom x-rl-tenant), 3) deterministic sampling and log-level rate-limiting, 4) tenant-aware routing and retention tagging, 5) add provenance metadata and signature for tamper detection. Out of scope: deep application-level parsing (that remains with service libs), long-term storage policy changes beyond tagging, and running ELK for all tenants (only compliance workspaces routed to ELK).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical schema doc published and linked in README; field mapping table for common service fields
Daemonset/sidecar and Vector pipeline deployed to staging collecting from 10 staging services with no message loss
All ingested logs include: timestamp, service_name, env, tenant_id (or tenant_unknown), request_id, trace_id (traceparent), log_level, and _ingest_prov fields
Dashboards in Grafana/Loki updated to use canonical fields and show trace-to-log linking for sampled traces
End-to-end latency for enrichment stage adds <= 2ms median and <= 10ms P99 under normal load in perf tests
Toggle to route compliance workspaces to ELK by tenant label implemented and tested
Automated integration test and a GitHub PR that validates field normalization for 6 sample log formats
Rollout plan documented including rollback steps and monitoring alerts for increased error or drop rates
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after incident where trace->log link was missing for payments flow. Included rough schema proposal. See design doc link below.

2025-02-14 - Tomas Nguyen: Spun up Vector pipeline PoC in personal k8s cluster. Preliminary results: able to attach traceparent and tenant headers via lua transform. Observed ~1.6ms median added latency. Sharing perf traces: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/poC-vector-20250214

2025-02-18 - Priya Sharma (infra review): Feedback - prefer daemonset enrichment for legacy apps that can't inject headers; ensure backpressure to avoid memory amplification. Recommend using gRPC batching with size limit and TTL.
2025-02-20 - Security (Liam O'Connor): Flagged requirement for signing _ingest_prov metadata when routing to ELK for compliance; suggested HMAC with KMS-stored key. Marked security_review_required.

2025-02-24 - Tomas Nguyen: Implemented tenant resolution fallback: header -> authenticated JWT claim -> host-metadata; added deterministic sampling based on trace_id modulo N. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/1897

2025-02-26 - Design review (Maya Lin): Approved schema mapping table; requested clearer names for request_id vs correlation_id. Decided to adopt 'request_id' as primary and keep correlation_id as deprecated alias for 6 months.

2025-02-27 - Observability (Eric Zhao): Dashboard changes merged; Loki queries updated to use tenant_id label and trace_id for joining with traces. Saved dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/observability/log-trace-join

2025-03-01 - Tomas Nguyen: Perf tests in staging with 2000 EPS sustained show P99 enrichment overhead ~9ms; preparing rollout to canary namespace. Next: implement canary routing and alerting for drop rate >0.1%
